name: Domo, Inc.

profile.description: Domo is a cloud-based business intelligence platform providing data integration, visualization, analytics, and AI-powered agent capabilities. The platform connects to hundreds of data sources and enables real-time dashboards, reporting, and AI agent workflows through its MCP Server and Agent Catalyst products. Founded in 2010 by Josh James (who previously founded Omniture, sold to Adobe for $1.8B), Domo went public in 2018 and is currently exploring strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Revenue has essentially flatlined at ~$318-319M from FY2024 to FY2026 (FY2026 ending Jan 31, 2026: $318.86M, up just 0.57% YoY), indicating stalled product-market expansion after earlier growth [1][2]. The company won CRN 2025 Products of the Year for BI and Data Analytics but market adoption has not translated to revenue growth. AI Deployment (1/2): Domo launched Agent Catalyst for building autonomous AI agents with governance, an AI Agent Builder, AI Library, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server connecting to OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude -- shipping real AI capabilities to customers [3][4]. Ben Schein was appointed Chief AI and Analytics Officer in May 2026 to drive AI beyond dashboards into live business workflows [3]. Market Share (0/2): Traditional BI market share is eroding as AI-native tools (ChatGPT data analysis, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini) reduce demand for legacy dashboarding; Seeking Alpha analysts argue 'AI is making this company obsolete' [5]. $156M market cap vs. multi-billion competitors signals a subscale position. Product Pipeline (1/2): AI-focused product additions (MCP Server, Agent Builder) are well-defined and shipping at Domopalooza/BUILD 2026, but the strategic alternatives process creates uncertainty about continued development under new ownership [6]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Significant R&D spending relative to revenue with 74.88% gross margin, consistent with a software company investing in platform evolution [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Domo's mission -- 'optimizes your business by connecting you to the data, people, and expertise you need to improve business results' -- is clear and specific to their domain but interchangeable with any BI/analytics peer. Josh James' broader vision of democratizing data access for 'everyone from the CEO to the front-line worker' adds some distinctiveness [7]. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of significant charitable programs, community investment, or foundation activity for a company of this size. As a co-founder of the ParityPledge, Domo is committed to interviewing at least one woman and one person of color for leadership positions, but this is a process commitment, not a community impact program [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor reviews report declining culture -- 'since the CEO returned, very little confidence in executive leadership,' forced return-to-office policies, and minimal pay increases outside executives [8]. Employee count dropped to 888, a 7.31% decline of 70 employees YoY, indicating workforce contraction [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Net insider selling dominates -- 14 of 15 recent insider transactions are sales, including CEO Josh James selling 96,088 shares and CFO selling 68,483 shares in June 2026, heavily outweighing James' earlier purchase of 13,025 shares for ~$166K [9]. This is clearly net insider selling, not neutral.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Domo has never achieved GAAP profitability in 14+ years, with FY2026 net loss of -$55.5M on $318.2M revenue [1][2]. D/E and ROE are excluded due to negative shareholders' equity (book value per share -$4.13). Forward P/E of 74.73 is above the 60 floor, scoring 0.0 [10]. Profit margin of -17.43% is below the 0% floor, scoring 0.0 [1]. Revenue growth YoY of 0.57% scores partial credit (0.687), and 5-year revenue CAGR of 7.49% scores well (0.833) [2]. The constructive metrics are 74.88% gross margin and positive TTM operating cash flow of $9.2M, though neither feeds directly into the infrastructure algorithm. Cash of $39.1M against $148.4M total debt with ongoing losses creates balance sheet pressure. Stock price ~$3.46 with avg daily volume of 1,880,718 yields ~$6.5M daily liquidity, passing the $1M floor [10].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): Domo's core BI platform faces direct AI substitution risk -- AI-native tools from Microsoft (Copilot), Google (Gemini), and ChatGPT's data analysis capabilities are commoditizing traditional dashboarding and data visualization, the exact functions Domo monetizes [5]. Seeking Alpha analysts explicitly argue AI is making the company obsolete. Revenue stagnation (0.57% YoY growth) corroborates that customers are not expanding Domo usage and may be churning to AI-powered alternatives. The strategic alternatives process itself may reflect the board's recognition that standalone survival is challenging in the AI era. CEO Josh James acknowledged that 'most companies have an execution problem more than an AI problem,' but execution has not translated to growth [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Domo is actively shipping AI capabilities -- Agent Catalyst, MCP Server, AI Agent Builder -- and appointed a Chief AI and Analytics Officer in May 2026, demonstrating meaningful adaptation even as the core threat remains existential [3][4].

infinite_game.summary: Domo shows mixed signals on infinite thinking. Founder Josh James built and sold Omniture to Adobe for $1.8B, then founded Domo with a vision of democratizing data access. But 14 years of consecutive losses, stalled growth, and the active exploration of a sale suggest the cause may not be sustainable. The strategic alternatives process is itself a finite action -- selling the company rather than continuing to build it. Heavy insider selling and deteriorating employee culture further undermine infinite game characteristics.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Making data work for everyone' reflects a genuine vision of democratized business intelligence that has guided Domo since founding in 2010 [7]. The company consistently pursued cloud-based BI when enterprise vendors dominated on-premise, showing commitment to the vision. However, 14 years without profitability and active exploration of a sale suggest the cause may not be commercially viable as articulated, and the vision has not survived a leadership transition or been tested through genuine crisis.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reviews describe deteriorating culture -- employees report 'very little confidence in most executive leadership' since the CEO returned, internal rumors contradicting public announcements, forced return-to-office, and minimal pay increases except for executives [8]. The workforce has shrunk to 888 employees (down 7.31% YoY). ISS Governance QualityScore of 10 (worst possible) with Compensation and Shareholder Rights pillar scores of 10 each signals significant governance concerns. Josh James' dual-class control (Class A shares with 40 votes each) means Domo qualifies as a Nasdaq 'controlled company' [6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence that Domo frames competition as an opportunity to improve. The company's positioning emphasizes its own platform capabilities rather than learning from Microsoft's Copilot, Tableau/Salesforce, or Google Looker. The finite nature of the competitive response -- exploring a sale rather than competing -- suggests a defensive rather than growth mindset [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Domo has pivoted its product strategy toward AI with Agent Catalyst, MCP Server integration, and the appointment of a Chief AI and Analytics Officer -- meaningful adaptation in response to the AI disruption threatening traditional BI [3][4]. The strategic alternatives process itself represents willingness to transform the company's ownership structure. However, revenue stagnation (0.57% growth) suggests these pivots have not yet translated to market traction [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Josh James has persisted with Domo through 14 years of losses, multiple capital raises, and an 81% stock price decline from $18.49 to $3.46. The decision to explore strategic alternatives in February 2026 took courage as it acknowledged the limits of the standalone path [6]. However, heavy insider selling (14 of 15 recent transactions are sales by CEO and CFO) dilutes the courage narrative and suggests leadership may be positioning for exits [9].

investment_thesis: Domo's primary investment thesis rests on a potential acquisition at a premium to the current ~$156M market cap. The board concluded in February 2026 that pursuing a strategic transaction represents the best path to maximize shareholder value, and is in advanced negotiations regarding a potential transaction [6]. At 0.49x Price/Sales with 74.88% gross margins and $437.9M subscription RPO (+8% YoY), the platform could be attractive to a strategic acquirer seeking BI/analytics capabilities enhanced by the new AI agent framework and MCP Server [1][3].
thesis_continued: However, independent of an acquisition, the fundamental picture is deeply challenging. Revenue has flatlined at ~$319M for three consecutive fiscal years, GAAP losses continue ($55.5M TTM), and AI-native tools are commoditizing the traditional BI market that generates Domo's revenue [5]. The $148.4M total debt against $39.1M cash creates balance sheet pressure with no visible path to standalone profitability. The ISS Governance QualityScore of 10 (worst possible), dual-class voting control by Josh James, and heavy insider selling (14 of 15 recent transactions) signal significant governance risk [6][9]. The stock has declined 81% from $18.49 to $3.46, reflecting the market's deep skepticism about standalone viability. If the strategic alternatives process fails to produce a transaction, the stock faces meaningful downside risk.
key_catalysts: Completion of strategic alternatives process with potential acquisition at a premium -- advanced negotiations disclosed in June 2026 could close in H2 2026 [6]
Record Q4 FY2026 billings of $111.2M (+8% YoY) and subscription RPO of $437.9M (+8%) could support a higher acquisition price [1]
AI product portfolio (Agent Catalyst, MCP Server, AI Agent Builder) could increase strategic value to potential acquirers seeking AI-enhanced analytics capabilities [3][4]
key_risks: Strategic alternatives process may not result in a transaction, leaving a subscale BI company with $148.4M debt, $39.1M cash, and ongoing losses with no path to profitability [6]

AI-native tools from Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and ChatGPT are commoditizing traditional BI dashboarding -- Domo's core revenue source -- with Seeking Alpha analysts arguing 'AI is making this company obsolete' [5]

ISS Governance QualityScore of 10 (worst), dual-class voting control, heavy insider selling (14 of 15 recent transactions), and declining employee satisfaction signal deep organizational challenges [6][8][9]
